title: WAYS TO SELL EXISTING CONSUMABLE PRODUCTS
content:
When you sell someone else's consumable, the most important comparison is not simply which method sounds easiest. It is what happens after the customer uses the product up.

With affiliate marketing, the customer may buy through your link once and make the next purchase somewhere else. With wholesale or resale, the customer needs to return to your store or business. With dropshipping, they need to return to you even though the supplier fulfills the order.

Some network-marketing or direct-selling structures work differently. A customer account may remain attributed to a seller, and qualifying future orders may continue to compensate that seller. Whether that happens, what the seller must do to remain eligible, and whether the retail economics are attractive all depend on the actual company and compensation plan.

DRAFT ROUTER QUESTIONS
When this customer needs the product again:
Where do they reorder?
Who controls the customer relationship?
Is the reorder attributed to me?
Do I get paid again?
What must I do to remain eligible?

NETWORK MARKETING / DIRECT SELLING → PDF 27.
AFFILIATE / REFERRAL → PDF 28.
WHOLESALE / RESALE → PDF 29.
DROPSHIPPING → PDF 30.
I WANT MY OWN CONSUMABLE → PDF 22.

COMPARE PURCHASE ONE, TWO, AND TEN
Network/direct selling may preserve seller attribution on qualifying customer reorders, depending on the actual plan. Affiliate programs may or may not preserve attribution. Resellers capture repeat purchases when customers return to their store. Dropshippers capture them when customers return through their storefront.

Do not compare only the first-sale commission or margin. Write out what happens on purchase one, purchase two, and purchase ten. Where does the customer go? Who owns the relationship? Who fulfills? Who gets paid? What must you do to remain eligible?

THREE-PURCHASE TEST
Take any opportunity and trace one customer.

Purchase 1: What did I do, what did the customer do, and how was I paid?
Purchase 2: Does the customer need me again? Does an account or tracking relationship persist?
Purchase 10: Assuming the customer still loves the product, what keeps the purchase connected to me?

A model that looks excellent on purchase one can look very different by purchase ten, and vice versa.

DO NOT LET "RECURRING" HIDE THE MECHANICS
A company may describe customers as recurring, preferred, subscribed, autoship, members, or something else. Those labels do not tell you whether YOU receive future compensation.

For every route in this section, reduce the model to plain language: "When this customer needs more, they do X. Because Y relationship still exists, I do or do not get paid again."

COMPARE THE REORDER PATH, NOT JUST THE FIRST COMMISSION

When you sell an existing consumable, the first transaction can make several models look deceptively similar. You recommend or offer a product, the customer buys it, and you earn something.

The differences become clearer on the next order.

With ordinary affiliate marketing, a later purchase may or may not remain attributed to you. It depends on the merchant and program rules.

With wholesale or resale, the customer can return to your store for another unit, but they are generally free to buy the same or an equivalent product elsewhere. Your business captures the reorder only if they return to you.

With dropshipping, the customer may return through your storefront while the supplier continues fulfilling the physical order. That can preserve the customer relationship, but supplier reliability matters every time the customer replenishes.

With some network-marketing or direct-selling structures, a customer account may remain connected to a particular seller and future qualifying purchases may continue generating compensation. Whether that actually happens, under what conditions, and for how long must be verified in the current plan.

THE AFFILIATE / NETWORK-MARKETING RELATIONSHIP

Affiliate marketing and network marketing are closer cousins than their reputations suggest. In both, you can recommend another company's product and receive compensation when a customer buys it. The major consumable-specific distinction to investigate is customer retention: after you introduce the customer, does that customer remain associated with you so later qualifying reorders can continue compensating you?

Ordinary affiliate tracking often centers on the transaction. Many direct-selling structures center more strongly on the customer account. Neither label guarantees a particular result, and some affiliate programs also provide recurring or persistent attribution, so verify the actual rules.

Network marketing may additionally include team-based compensation. That is a second layer of the model, not a reason to ignore the underlying retail customer economics.

The goal is not to declare one model universally better. It is to understand which model actually creates the repeat relationship you thought you were choosing when you chose a consumable.

A $50 MONTHLY CONSUMABLE UNDER FOUR ARRANGEMENTS

Imagine a customer likes a product enough to spend $50 every month for a year. Their total retail purchasing is $600.

That does NOT mean every seller connected to that product earns from $600.

An affiliate might earn only from the first attributed transaction, or might earn on later transactions if the program explicitly preserves attribution. A reseller can earn a retail margin each time the customer chooses to return to that reseller. A dropship store can potentially capture repeat orders placed through its storefront while continuing to rely on the supplier for fulfillment. A direct-selling arrangement may compensate future qualifying customer orders if the account remains connected to the seller and the seller remains eligible.

Notice what we are not doing: comparing hypothetical profit percentages and declaring a winner. Actual margins, fees, shipping, returns, qualifications, customer behavior, and program terms vary.

We are identifying the mechanism. Once you understand the mechanism, you know which facts need to be researched for a real opportunity.

A FAST WAY TO CHOOSE WHICH MODEL TO EXPLORE FIRST

Ask which sentence sounds most like you.

"I want customers to remain associated with me when they reorder, and I am willing to evaluate a direct-selling company and its compensation structure." Start with NETWORK MARKETING/DIRECT SELLING.

"I want to recommend products without becoming the retailer, and I am comfortable with whatever repeat-purchase attribution the actual affiliate program provides." Start with AFFILIATE MARKETING.

"I want to buy inventory and be the retailer that customers return to." Start with WHOLESALE/RESELLING.

"I want customers to buy from my store, but I want a supplier to hold and ship the inventory." Start with DROPSHIPPING.

These are starting points, not endorsements. The individual opportunity still has to survive the deeper evaluation in the next guide.

THE DECISION

The four models differ most in who owns the retail transaction, who carries inventory or fulfillment responsibility, and whether a customer's later purchases remain economically connected to you. Choose the mechanism you want to investigate, then evaluate a real opportunity using its actual terms.

WHERE TO GO NEXT
Choose the route based on what happens on the reorder, not only what looks attractive on the first sale: PDF 27 network/direct selling, PDF 28 affiliate, PDF 29 resale, or PDF 30 dropshipping.
